column1: The exact form of the CIA constraint depends on which transactions or purchases are subject to the CIA requirements. For example, both consumption goods and investment goods might be subject to the requirement. Or only consumption might be subject to the constraint. Or only a subset of all consumption goods may require cash for their purchase. The constraint will also depend on what constitutes cash. Can bank deposits that earn interest, for example, also be used to carry out transactions? The exact specification of the transactions subject to the CIA constraint can be important.
